answer: Each identity opens one thread and locks a 60-credit bond. The thread is sealed with a unique crystal seal whose serial is published. At the zenith checkpoint, an auditor recomputes the crystal seal checksum and checks the seal belongs to that thread; a mismatch burns the bond and bars the identity. The filing fee for the k-th thread is 25+5(k-1), so the 1000th costs 5020 and 1000 fakes pay 2,522,500 in fees plus 60,000 locked. An honest identity pays only 85 for one thread. A rented-seal ring fails because a seal bound to another thread id fails the zenith checksum.
